SELECT 
  fish_date_doy,
  cls,
  COUNT(*) as trips,
  SUM(yt) as total_yt,
  SUM(anglers) as total_anglers,
  ROUND(SUM(yt)::float / SUM(anglers)::float, 2) as yt_per_angler
FROM trips
WHERE avail_season = 6 
  AND fish_date_doy >= 60 
  AND fish_date_doy <= 91
GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls
ORDER BY fish_date_doy, cls
LIMIT 100

SELECT 
  fish_date_doy,

  SUM(yt) as total_yt,
  SUM(anglers) as total_anglers,
  ROUND(SUM(yt)::float / SUM(anglers)::float, 2) as yt_per_angler
FROM trips
WHERE avail_season = 6 
  AND fish_date_doy >= 88
GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls
ORDER BY fish_date_doy, cls

SELECT 
  fish_date_doy,
  boat,
  cls,
  COUNT(*) as count
FROM schedule
WHERE avail_season = 6 
  AND fish_date_doy >= 92
  AND fish_date_doy <= 106
GROUP BY fish_date_doy, boat, cls
ORDER BY fish_date_doy, boat, cls
LIMIT 80

import pandas as pd

# Check boat performance D71-91 (the peak window I missed)
trips = tables['trips']
peak_window = trips[(trips['fished_date_season'] == 6) & 
                     (trips['fished_date_doy'].between(71, 91))]

# Group by boat and class
boat_perf = peak_window.groupby(['boat', 'cls']).agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum'
}).reset_index()
boat_perf['yt_per_angler'] = boat_perf['yt'] / boat_perf['anglers']
boat_perf = boat_perf.sort_values('yt_per_angler', ascending=False)

print("=== BEST BOATS D71-D91 ===")
print(boat_perf.head(20).to_string())
